With this information, we can start calculating... If we know that you jump with some velocity (v0) on Pluto, and that produces some maximum jump height (y1) on Pluto, and we know that you'll have a velocity of zero at the height of your jump, then we get this by using the second equation:

0 = v0 + g·t

So we can determine the "jump/flight" time for Pluto as:

t = - v0/g

Now, when you plug in the zero initial height (y0) and the t into the first equation I gave you, you get:

y1 = 0 + v0·(- v0/g) + 0.5·g·(- v0/g)

Which you can simplify as:

y1 = - v02/g - 0.5·v0
